macro_context.market_sentiment: Cautiously positive on May 5 — S&P 500 +0.77%, Nasdaq +1.00%, Russell 2000 +1.41% — recovering from May 4 sell-off driven by Middle East escalation. Oil eased from spike highs (WTI $104.10, -2.22%) as U.S.-Iran conflict uncertainty persists but a deal remains on the table per Defense Secretary Hegseth.
macro_context.fed_outlook: FOMC held rates at 3.50%–3.75% on April 29, 2026 (third consecutive hold, 8-4 dissent vote — highest since October 1992). Market pricing zero cuts in 2026 and one 25 bp cut in December 2027; elevated energy-driven inflation cited as key constraint. Powell's term as chair is ending.
macro_context.geopolitical: Middle East conflict (U.S.-Iran) is the dominant risk driver — UAE intercepted missiles from Iran on May 4, sending oil surging and equities lower. Broader backdrop includes tariff uncertainty, U.S. intervention in Venezuela, NATO posture in Greenland, and midterm elections. IMF April 2026 WEO flagged 'Global Economy Tested Again' amid elevated geopolitical risk.

ticker_news.headline: Amazon launches Amazon Supply Chain Services, opening its logistics network to all businesses — described as 'AWS of Logistics'; UPS and FedEx shares fell 8-9% on the news
Amazon Q1 2026 beat: worldwide net sales $181.5B (~2% above consensus), AWS revenue $37.6B ahead of expectations, backlog surged 50% QoQ to ~$365B (ex-Anthropic deal)
BNP Paribas analyst Nick Jones raised AMZN price target post-Q1, citing accelerating AI-driven demand and improving financial outlook; maintains Buy
OpenAI deepens partnership with Amazon AWS, shifting aggressively away from Microsoft Azure — companies with large AWS commitments can more easily adopt OpenAI models
AMZN stock up ~0.65% in premarket May 5 at $273.82, trading near 52-week high of $276.10

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Strong buy consensus: 41-47 analysts covering AMZN, 45 Buy / 2 Hold / 0 Sell. Stifel set $319 target on May 1, 2026 (maintained Buy). BNP Paribas raised target post-Q1 beat. DA Davidson was the last downgrader (Feb 6, 2026, target cut to $175 — outlier). Price target range: $175 low / $370 high; cluster $295–$320. Analysts cite AWS AI backlog surge (+50% QoQ) and logistics expansion as catalysts. Multiple sources see 20–30%+ upside from current ~$274.

web_context.competitor_activity: UPS and FedEx took immediate hits (-8 to -9%) from Amazon Supply Chain Services launch, signaling Amazon is entering their core market with a structural cost advantage. In cloud, Microsoft Azure remains the closest AWS rival, but OpenAI's pivot toward AWS deepens Amazon's AI ecosystem moat at Microsoft's expense. In e-commerce, Walmart, AliExpress, eBay, and Etsy remain relevant but none threatening AWS/logistics dominance. The OpenAI-AWS partnership announced April 29 is a material competitive win over Microsoft.
web_context.earnings_info: Q1 2026 reported April 29, 2026: EPS $2.78 (beat), revenue $181.5B (~2% beat), AWS $37.6B (beat), backlog ~$365B (+50% QoQ). Next earnings: Q2 2026, estimated ~July 30, 2026 (unconfirmed, after market). Q2 2026 EPS estimate: $1.82; revenue estimate: $188.96B.
